content.title: About
content.content: Taquito are small Mexican turnovers made from corn or wheat flour, filled with seasoned beef or pork, vegetables and spices. They are traditionally pan‑fried or baked, giving a crisp shell and juicy filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Taquitos originated in Mexico in the 19th century as street food.
The name comes from the Spanish word “taco”, meaning “snack”.
Original recipes use only corn flour, but wheat versions are now common.
They are often served with salsa, guacamole and lime wedges.
In some regions they are nicknamed “little boats” because of their shape.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef and pork provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat is rich in B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Fiber from the tortilla
items.content: Corn flour adds a modest amount of dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: Taquitos fit moderate low‑carb diets, especially when made with corn flour.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat‑based taquitos contain gluten and are unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Pork and beef can be high in saturated fats; consumption should be moderate.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked meat may harbor pathogens; ensure thorough cooking.

items.title: Salt and seasoning
items.content: Fillings often contain added salt or soy sauce, increasing sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Taquitos are best enjoyed hot, straight from the pan or oven, with dips such as salsa, guacamole or sour cream and fresh vegetables. Their handheld shape makes them ideal for snacks or buffet stations.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked taquitos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. They can be frozen for up to a month; reheat in the oven or skillet before serving to restore crispness.
